current.text: Jaylen Brown is gone. Boston now has Jayson Tatum back for a full season, plus Paul George and Mitchell Robinson.
Boston should be a better and deeper regular season team than last season.
The new roster does not clearly improve Boston's title chances.
One analyst predicts 48 wins because the East is tougher and fewer teams will tank. The win total of 51.5 ranks 4th in the league, so a late-season tank is unlikely.

The starting lineup is not settled. The newest expert projection starts Derrick White, Baylor Scheierman, Jayson Tatum, Paul George and Neemias Queta. It has Pritchard, Hauser, Robinson, Walsh and Conley off the bench. The current depth chart starts Pritchard instead of Scheierman.
The team is very deep, with at least 12 rotation-level players. In a 10-man rotation, Jordan Walsh or another player will sit most nights. Ron Harper Jr. is outside the rotation.
Boston has 14 players on the roster and one open two-way slot.
Paul George is clearly the number two option behind Jayson Tatum.
Payton Pritchard's path to usage is more crowded than last season. Tatum, George and White are ahead of him, and Tatum and George fill Brown's role, so he gains no extra opportunity.
Brown's heavy ball use may have pushed teammates into bad late-clock shots. Tatum and George share the ball more, which could help the shooting of Pritchard and White.
The plan is to play less five-out and put four shooters around a big man in the dunker spot. Tatum will play only some small-ball center.
The supporting cast has clearer roles than last season, which should make it easier to fit in George and Robinson.
Boston has 16 back-to-backs, tied with Brooklyn for the most in the league.
The many back-to-backs mainly hurt Paul George and Mitchell Robinson, who are likely to sit some of them.
The fantasy playoff schedule is 4-3-4, for 11 games. That is one game short of the maximum and ranks 4th in the league. The window includes 3 back-to-backs.

durable.text: Boston gets a lot out of players with limited offense, such as Jordan Walsh.

tags.name: many back-to-backs
tags.detail: 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. This mainly affects Paul George and Mitchell Robinson.
tags.new_meaning: The team has one of the highest back-to-back counts this season, so rest risk for its fragile or veteran players is higher.

tags.name: deep rotation
tags.detail: At least 12 rotation-level players for about 10 spots. Walsh, Harper Jr. and the bench wings lose minutes.
tags.new_meaning: The team has more rotation-level players than minutes, so bench and fringe players get fewer or less stable minutes.

tags.name: contender
tags.detail: Win total of 51.5 ranks 4th. Experts see a better regular season team than last year.
tags.new_meaning: The team is expected to be among the stronger regular season teams, so the risk of tanking or late-season shutdowns is low.

note: Tatum and George are the clear top two usage options. Pritchard loses opportunity, and the deep rotation of at least 12 players caps bench players like Hauser, Walsh and Conley. Boston is tied for the most back-to-backs (16) and has 3 in our playoff window, so George and Robinson carry extra rest risk, though the 11 playoff games rank 4th. Early on, watch who wins the open starting spots at wing (Scheierman or Pritchard) and center (Queta or Robinson).
